messages:
Mara: Noticed a weird keyboard flow in compact dashboard table. When opening overflow (⋯) the Tab moves focus to header instead of to the menu items. Figma: https://figma.com/file/redwood/compact-actions-2026

Jonah: Which browser/os? I tested earlier on Windows/Edge and it looked fine.

Mara: macOS/Chrome. Steps: Tab to the action cell, press Space to open, first item gets focus briefly, but next Tab escapes to topbar.

Sam: sounds like our menu is rendered in a portal far away from the trigger. Chrome's sequential focus follows DOM order, not visual order.

Priya: we also have a touch target problem — icon-only action buttons are under 44px in compact rows. Mobile UX flagged by support.

Jonah: quick fix idea: when opening, move the menu DOM node to immediately follow the trigger element (still absolutely positioned). That preserves DOM order. Also add an explicit call to focus() on the first menuitem when the menu opens.

Sam: agree. Also add role="menu" and role="menuitem" semantics and manage arrow-key navigation inside the menu so Tab can still move out if users expect it, but arrow keys stay inside.

Mara: copy/context: the overflow tooltip currently says "More". Can we change to "Actions" and SR label to "Actions for <row title>" so screen readers announce context?

Priya: spacing token note: add spacing.icon-action: 8px padding (token name: spacing.icon-action-compact) so min hit area becomes 44x44. That will affect several places; created a quick token PR draft.

Jonah: CSS proposal:
```
.action-icon {
  padding: 8px; /* token: spacing.icon-action-compact */
  min-height: 44px;
  min-width: 44px;
}
.menu--portal {
  position: absolute;
  left: 0; top: 0; /* positioned by JS */
}
```

Sam: for keyboard, implement:
- on open: menuEl.setAttribute('aria-expanded','true'); menuEl.querySelector('[role=menuitem]').focus();
- use keydown handler for ArrowUp/ArrowDown to move focus among items
- use focusout with short debounce to close if focus leaves the menu for good

Mara: good. Priya, can you run a quick touch-target sweep in the next token PR? Also check table dense variant separately since tokens differ.

Priya: will do. I'll include screenshots of before/after on iOS Safari and Android Chrome.

DesignBot: automated-check: when PR is opened please run accessibility-suite (axe) and tag @Mara @Sam on failures.

Jonah: I'll add unit tests for focus order and an e2e simulating keyboard nav opening and tabbing through menu + returning to next cell.

Mara: plan: Sam opens the implementation PR with JS focus management + menu DOM placement, Priya opens token PR for spacing.icon-action-compact, Jonah adds tests, I'll verify SR labels and close after product sign-off. Thanks everyone.
